answer: Three tasters judge the cup blind, and each stakes his post on the verdict written beside the lot number. A ripple lot passed off as tasted fails the verdict: the tasters must have sipped at the zephyr of the cupping, and a lot never tasted has no note at all. Staging a false tasting costs a forger 16,300 in bribes to tasters who would lose their posts, and the nectar verdict in the cupping book follows the lot, so a lot whose tea was never judged cannot be sold.
